Splice two sensors into one consistent series

Source: R/splice.R
ntl_splice.Rd

Puts an older series (from, e.g. Suomi NPP VNP46A3) on the scale of a newer one (to, e.g. NOAA-20 VJ146A3) using the periods both observe, and reports level shifts per unit so you can judge whether the splice is innocuous or a research problem in itself.

Usage

ntl_splice(
  x,
  from,
  to,
  value = "ntl_sum",
  id_col = NULL,
  method = c("ratio", "regression", "none"),
  overlap = NULL,
  by_month = FALSE,
  switch_at = NULL,
  fill_gaps = FALSE,
  min_overlap = 3,
  min_share_valid = NULL
)

Arguments

x

An ntl_long data frame (from ntl_extract()) holding both series, e.g. rbind() of two extractions.

from, to

Series names (column series).

value

Outcome column to calibrate.

id_col

Unit identifier column.

method

"ratio", "regression" or "none".

overlap

Optional overlap window used for estimation: two periods (start and end) or a vector of periods. Defaults to every period both series observe.

by_month

Estimate a separate calibration for each calendar month (monthly data). Useful at high latitude, where the two satellites' summer coverage differs. Needs several years of overlap: with fewer, each factor rests on one or two months per unit.

switch_at

First period taken from to. Defaults to the first period in which to has data.

fill_gaps

Fill missing to values after the switch with adjusted from values.

min_overlap

Minimum overlap observations per calibration group.

min_share_valid

Only use overlap observations where both series have at least this coverage share for estimation.

Value

An ntl_long data frame with one series named "<from>+<to>" and a column origin saying where each value came from. The calibration diagnostics are in ntl_splice_report().

Details

Calibration is estimated per unit (and per calendar month if by_month = TRUE) on overlap periods where both series are observed:

  • "ratio": to = k * from, with k = sum(to) / sum(from). Multiplicative, so it also applies to means and adjusted sums.

  • "regression": to = a + b * from by OLS; adjusted values are floored at zero.

  • "none": no adjustment; series are simply stacked.

Units with fewer than min_overlap overlap observations (or no light in from) fall back to the pooled calibration and are flagged in the diagnostics.

The spliced series uses adjusted from values before switch_at and to values from switch_at on, so the sensor never alternates from one period to the next. With fill_gaps = TRUE, missing to values after the switch are filled with adjusted from values where available.

Examples

ex <- ntl_example()
m <- ntl_files(ex$dir, "eog_vnl_monthly")
m <- m[m$period >= as.Date("2022-04-01") &
         m$period <= as.Date("2023-03-01"), ]
long <- ntl_extract(m, ex$units_old, id_col = "district", quiet = TRUE)
sp <- ntl_splice(long,
  from = "eog_vnl_monthly_npp", to = "eog_vnl_monthly_j01"
)
head(sp)
